reason: Muddled and abstract: 'My paint will not stick' / 'The paint is wet now' do not connect, and 'Tomorrow we will call it yesterday' is a riddle beyond this age.
Name switches between 'Claare' and 'Claire', and the ironic joke 'That is the best soup I never ate' goes over a 3-4-year-old's head.
Confusing narrator aside: 'She sang, "Mary had a little sheep." Well, she sang "lamb," but close.'
The second half gets tangled and abstract: 'Ten blocks, one cracker... Ten is one and zero. That one goes first.'
Confusing abstract category idea for this age: 'Now it is with the fruits and the foods at the same time.'
Contradictory plot: 'That one is the other team's net!' is the wrong net, then 'It went right into the other team's net. "Goal!"'
Confusing sequence and forced line: she zips her coat, then 'picked up her coat from the hook'; 'We can dream of carrots on the bus.'
Confusing jump to an abstract idea: 'A week is seven days. You need more fingers.'
Confusing plot: a 'little backyard pool' has 'Nina the lifeguard' in a 'tall chair', and the ending 'Can I chase you to the door?' goes nowhere.
Unsafe behaviour not addressed: 'Athena ran after it... She could not see Dad anymore', and Dad only says 'There you are' with no reminder to stay close.
Abstract season idea hard to follow: 'So the team was all of it. Every practice. Every game. From the first line to the last line.' plus 'chlorine', 'schedule'.
Confusing plot: the box 'does not move' yet later 'he pushes his tower slowly across the rug', and 'Now the box is a big, round bottom' is hard to picture.
Counting muddle confuses the lesson: crayon put back yet counts four, then 'One crayon less, one number less.' and 'Now we both have four'.
Wandering plot (lost teddy, puddle, socks) with forced words: 'She looked in the slow toy train' and 'rolled the slow train, early for teddy's tea party'.
Confusing mixed setting: soccer on TV at an ice rink, 'The horn at the rink beeped too, for the ice skaters.'
Abstract, contradictory concept for age 3: '"That is Hebrew," he said.' then Margot 'opened her book from the right'.
Confusing sequence: batter is stirred but never baked, then 'He tried to spread it on his bread.'
Muddled time concept: counting to Saturday always gives seven, 'Seven days make a week... So Saturday comes after all seven days?'
Idioms and adult concepts: 'cook up a plan', 'late fee', 'Tomorrow would be too late.'
Abstract day-counting too hard for age 3: 'And five more days after that... Seven days. That is a whole week.'
Abstract time reasoning: 'After you sleep tonight, today will be called yesterday' and 'tomorrow, his digging day would be yesterday'; the rain-filled hole also contradicts the dry night.
Unexplained adult sadness: 'A tear ran down her father's cheek' and 'Why was her father crying?' is never answered.

Perspective reasoning too abstract for age 4: 'She walked far away from the clock. The clock looked small now, small like the button!', plus confusing 'a circle that was alive' and 'paid her one red crayon'.
Garbled and scattered: 'He climbed no.', 'It is almost late for snack time', and a nose-hole mirror detour that breaks the plot.
Confusing forced word plus fire content: 'Papa lit a small fire in the big lamp. No, wait, Papa turned on the lamp.'
Geometry too abstract and story too long for age 3: 'The block had six faces... the curved skin of the ball. A square sticker likes a flat face.'
Confusing plot: 'His marks looked just like the other marks' leads to the plane at the neighbor's door with no clear reason, all in one long paragraph.
Lecture line 'Sunscreen helps protect your skin from sunburn.' plus the confusing 'The windy day pushes them' and a plot with no clear focus.
Confusing viewpoint idea ('From the floor, she could see her mom's knees') and a 4-year-old who 'jumped a little jump into the water' with no grown-up beside her.
The ending makes no sense: 'That throw was a little messy,' Milo said, pointing at his own shoes. Hudson had stepped in a puddle from the rain (inside a gym).
Confusing plot: the truck 'sat inside a big box on the shelf' but the box holds only a pillow, then the truck appears anyway.
Wandering plot with an abstract re-sorting idea: 'The same blocks, but in a new way!' and 'Same books, different shelves!'
Tangled letter logic: 'The round part of the b faced the same way as his right hand' for a word written 'DOG', plus a feather from the dog's tail.

Many long sentences, e.g. 'But when she got to the sink, she scrubbed for two seconds and turned off the water.' and 'The germs could still hide in her soapy fingers, and germs made teeth and tummies sick.'
Abstract category overlap for age 3: 'The apple sat in both groups at once.' with labels and 'It fits two ways'.
Implied death theme a 3-4-year-old may not follow: 'Ivy sat on the grass by Grandpa Joe's stone' and 'Bye, Grandpa Joe'.
Confusing cause and effect: 'But the red came out brown and muddy' from a yellow-tipped brush, then the same red on yellow 'made orange'.
Confusing premise: a school nap turns into night, 'The moon was up. It was still night,' then scenes wander (letters, 'Slimy' cup, snail).
Abstract metaphor and unfamiliar words: 'build a tall tower of sounds' and 'I am your audience today,' plus a 'concert' and 'violin' tangent.
Confusing and hard words: 'the cold stethoscope' and tasting grape from 'a sweet sticker,' then a separate dark-room search.
Rambling and confusing letter talk: '"And what does M say?" asked Miss Po. "For Miss Po, my name."' and 'like my foot going mmm down the hall.'
Disjointed plot jumps from playground slides to a drum by a sleeping baby to 'She sniffed her shoe. "My sock is smelly!"' with no single thread.
Unsafe behaviour left uncorrected: Sara, with no adult present, goes into 'a little house' where 'A kind man opened the door', then walks home alone.
Confusing letter sequence: 'He wrote J, then A, then S. Then he wrote a big M and another A.' The E is never mentioned and the fix is unclear.
Confusing shape logic: 'She had turned one square sideways... It has a point at the top!' is followed by an unexplained 'triangle roof'.
Confusing dialogue: 'No, silly. Five is me, next year.' from a seven-year-old, plus forced 'Her voice felt upset'.
Long and dense for a 3-year-old, with 'navy', 'pale', 'Lightest first, darkest last' and a confusing 'snow cloud, all white and pale' drawn in blue.
Muddled subplot the child cannot follow: 'Mia picked up a toothbrush. "Oops," said Mia. "That one is Aurora's."'
Running on a wet floor is shown as fun and never corrected: 'Drip, drip, drip went his feet on the floor. "Slip, slip!" he laughed.'
Muddled, abstract sense counting: 'Big kids know five whole senses. Sofia knew only one.' then 'Three senses!' after four are shown, and the last sense is left unnamed.
Abstract time counting muddles the plot: 'How many days until Saturday?... Seven fingers. Seven days.' then 'Ten, nine, eight, seven' for pancakes.
Tangled plot: Mason finds the monkey in the bush, then 'The bus driver did,' said Grandma, 'He knocked on the door.'
Right-to-left reading in another language is abstract and confuses the front-to-back idea: 'It is in Hebrew... We read it from right to left.'
Letter-reversal reading is beyond a 3-year-old listener: 'That says bog!' ... 'The round parts did not face the same way.'
Confusing opening and non sequitur: 'He could not leave it alone at home' (toy is lost in the car) and 'Maybe we can sell cookies at the big sale.'
Running off out of Dad's sight is never corrected and the story ends 'Again!'; ball 'rolled all the way back, lazy and slow, in the wind' is confusing.
Confusing flashback and abstract idea: 'Mom had given Ben a puzzle book. Ben had said thank you to Mom first.' and 'The words went back and forth, like a ball.'
Unsafe behaviour left uncorrected: 'He tried to shake the shelf a little.'
Tangled plot that jumps from sorting to a missing hat: 'Pip hung the red coat on a hook, but the hat shelf was empty.'
Counting muddle after giving a block away: 'Now we both have six.' Also forced 'Mia's lip began to melt into a sad face.'
Confusing plot at the counter: 'She grabbed at it, but the man did not hand it over. Avery remembered.'
Abstract chain of reasoning: 'He remembered when sand got in his shoe. He could not say "ow." So he cried too... Maybe crying was her way of asking.'
Confusing logic: counting to 'Twenty-six!' does not help, then the 'stick and a loop' letter is suddenly 'M'.
Confusing event: 'A wet spoon had sat on the paper. Where Jackson wrote, the letters turned dark blue!'
Confusing scene: 'One, two, three colors!' followed by four paints, and 'She pushed her swing high first, then she got to work.'
Forced required word makes a long, confusing sentence: 'Then he saw a tiny worm stick out its tongue-less face, and behind it, another sprout, and another.'
Confusing plot: a bus brings the boxes, but the ending says 'The truck came soon, just like the man said!'
Contradictory plot: the driver gives the cow back, then 'The toy cow sat on the desk, waiting for him.'
Confusing shape logic after the bite: 'Now the corner was gone. He counted again. "One, two, three."'
Adult-style reasoning and explanation: 'The sun was low, not high. So it was not morning.' plus the idiom 'paid close attention'.
